characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM JEOL 2100 operated at an acceleration voltage of 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol at −30 °C and 30 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 11(a) BF micrograph shows large α grains containing dark dislocation lines and bend contours separated by a bright, curved boundary κ band; Fig. 11(b) SADP: α along z = [001] with (-110), (110); κ along z = [1-12] with (220), (111).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Boundary κ-carbide between large α grains in the 1100 °C annealed specimen
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm the κ-carbide along α/α boundaries in the specimen annealed at 1100 °C
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (bright-field imaging and selected-area diffraction, SADP)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Quanta 450 operated at an acceleration voltage of 20 kV; specimens mechanically polished and etched in 8% Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 6(g) shows further coarsened α and γ grains with wavy boundaries, no resolvable matrix κ-carbide; Fig. 10(c) (5 µm scale bar) shows a bright boundary junction labelled 'boundary κ' with sub-micrometre white particles and a few dark pits in the grains.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RD–TD section of the 1100 °C, 1 h specimen
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure and boundary areas of the 1100 °C specimen

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku, D/Max-RB with a Cu target operated at 40 kV and 150 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1100 °C, 1 h pattern contains α- and γ-related reflections; κ-carbide reflections are present only in the 700, 800 and 850 °C specimens and absent from HR, 900 °C and higher-temperature (including 1100 °C) patterns.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 2θ = 30–90°; annealed specimens including the 1100 °C, 1 h condition
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and lattice parameter determination

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss AxioCam MRc5; specimens mechanically polished and etched in 8% Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded structure persists after annealing and becomes less contiguous at higher temperatures; applies to the annealed specimen set.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RD–ND and RD–TD sections of annealed specimens
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine banded structure and phase areas

characterization_methods.key_findings: Density about 6.80 g/cm³, ~13% lower than pure Fe.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the density of the steel

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Composition of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel; fractions of equilibrium phases (ferrite α, austenite γ and κ-carbide κ) calculated for temperatures above 550 °C
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD equilibrium phase-diagram (phase fraction vs temperature) calculation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated κ-carbide dissolution (eutectoid) temperature ~823 °C is lower than the experimentally measured dissolution temperature of between 850 °C and 900 °C; differences attributed to a non-equilibrium state and to atomic-fraction vs volume-fraction comparison.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation substructure / bend contours in α matrix
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: TEM bright-field image shows large α-matrix grains containing dark dislocation lines and broad dark bend-contour bands separated by a bright boundary band of κ-carbide.

interfaces.interface_notes: The boundary κ-carbide along large α grains cannot be detected by XRD, probably because its fraction is too small.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 1100 °C κ-carbide has dissolved during annealing (dissolution temperature between 850 °C and 900 °C); the boundary κ-carbide observed along α/α boundaries is believed to form during quenching when the annealing temperature is above the κ dissolution temperature.

phase_interfaces.coherence: TEM SADP recorded from the boundary κ-carbide and α matrix in the 1100 °C specimen: α along z = [001] with (-110) and (110) reflections; κ along z = [1-12] with (220) and (111) reflections (an N–W orientation relationship is explicitly reported only for the 1200 °C boundary κ)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 20 kg ingot of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was heated to 1200 °C and forged to a forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm.
Homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.
Hot-rolled to a plate of 3 mm thickness with the finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled to plate of 3 mm thickness

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After hot rolling the plate was water quenched to about 300 °C, then air cooled.
The hot-rolled plate was annealed at 1100 °C for 1 h. This is the sample-defining annealing condition (aliases: specimen annealed at 1100 °C, 1100 °C specimen).
The annealed plate was water quenched (annealing followed by water quenching).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Room-temperature tensile test on a universal testing machine (CMT 4105); tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction; specimen machined from the annealed and water quenched plate.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage length 50 mm and gage width 12.5 mm

strain_hardening_rate.description: For specimens annealed at or over 900 °C (no obvious κ-carbide in the matrix, including the 1100 °C specimen), the work hardening rates are lower than those of specimens annealed at 700–850 °C when true strain is less than about 5%.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve of the 1100 °C, 1 h specimen is shown in Fig. 15(a); true stress–true strain and work hardening rate curves in Fig. 15(b). Higher-temperature curves lie below lower-temperature curves.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Average grain size of γ, α2 (banded shape) and α1 (mainly among γ grains) increases with annealing temperature; θ/α2 and γ coarsen strongly above 900 °C; no numeric value is printed at 1100 °C (values reported only at 900 and 1200 °C: γ 5.5→36.0 μm, α2 26.1→68.4 μm for 900→1200 °C).

phases_present.morphology: banded (continuous, large grains, α2) plus fine grains mainly distributed among γ grains (α1); α grains coarsened
grains that coarsen with increasing temperature
phases_present.volume_fraction: changes only in the small range of 57% to 63% when the annealing temperature is between 900 °C and 1200 °C

phases_present.crystal_structure: perovskite structure based on FCC, space group Pm3m (κ lattice parameter 3.76–3.79 Å)
phases_present.morphology: no obvious κ-carbide resolvable in the matrix at 1100 °C; boundary κ-carbide present as thin bright intergranular film along some large α-grain boundaries

precipitates.distribution: distributed along some boundaries between large α grains in the α area, believed to form during quenching

structures.number_of_phases: 3 (ferrite α, austenite γ, κ-carbide including boundary κ)
structures.overall_structure: After annealing at 1100 °C for 1 h and water quenching the microstructure is basically composed of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide; the banded structure remains after annealing. When the annealing temperature is between 900 °C and 1100 °C no obvious κ-carbide is seen in the matrix (SEM) while the α and γ grain sizes increase apparently; boundary κ-carbide formed during quenching is present along some boundaries between large α grains.

unmapped_findings: Product of strength and ductility for the 1100 °C, 1 h specimen = 8 GPa% (Table 1).
For the 1100 °C, 1 h specimen the tensile properties in Table 1 are: ultimate strength 671 MPa, yield strength 518 MPa, ultimate elongation 12%, product of strength and ductility 8 GPa%.

The work hardening rate curves of specimens annealed at or over 900 °C (no obvious matrix κ-carbide, including the 1100 °C specimen) are lower than those of the 700–850 °C specimens when true strain is less than about 5%.

TEM analysis (not shown) indicates no obvious superlattice spots in the SADPs of α or γ phase in all the annealed specimens; ordering of atoms in α or γ is not expected during annealing at 700–1200 °C for 1 h.
No obvious TRIP or TWIP phenomenon was found during the tensile test of the annealed specimens.
The 1100 °C, 1 h specimen is one of eight annealing conditions (700, 800, 850, 900, 950, 1000, 1100, 1200 °C for 1 h) studied for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel.
The boundary κ-carbide along large α grains in specimens annealed at or over 900 °C cannot be detected by XRD, probably because its fraction is too small.
